title: Final Report of the Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack on the United States Capitol
pinpoint: Committee staff listing; report issued December 22, 2022
proposition: David B. Buckley was Staff Director, Timothy J. Heaphy Chief Investigative Counsel, and Denver Riggleman Senior Technical Advisor.

title: H. Res. 503, 117th Congress, as adopted June 30, 2021
proposition: The select committee had specific legislative-investigative purposes, subpoena and deposition powers, extended questioning authority, records/staffing arrangements and termination provisions, but could not mark up legislation.

title: Inside the January 6 Investigation, interview with Timothy Heaphy
pinpoint: January 19, 2023 transcript; five investigative teams discussion and discussion of DOJ requests for congressional witness interview records
proposition: Firsthand account of color-coded teams and the sequencing/investigation-integrity concerns surrounding transcript disclosure. Attributed personal account rather than official organizational instrument.

title: Committee on House Administration, Committee Rules, 119th Congress
pinpoint: Deposition authority procedures, paragraphs 1-10 and incorporation-by-reference provision
proposition: Reproduces deposition notice/consultation, joint-investigation attendance, questioning, privilege, transcript correction, certification and release procedures; controlling regulations must be checked.

title: House Committee on Rules, 119th Congress Regulations
pinpoint: Staff Deposition Authority Regulations and Remote Witness Participation Regulations links
proposition: Official directory for the 119th Congress deposition and remote-witness regulations.

title: U.S. Constitution, Twentieth Amendment
proposition: Congressional terms start at noon January 3 and Congress assembles January 3 unless a different day is appointed by law; these do not guarantee completed House organization by January 6.

title: U.S. House, Positions with Members and Committees
pinpoint: Individual employing offices, background screening and HVAPS sections
proposition: Members and committees are employing offices; recruitment services do not themselves possess hiring authority.

title: Committees' Congressional Handbook
proposition: Committee chairs exercise employment authority within applicable rules, employee ceilings apply, and consultant arrangements require prescribed approval and conditions.

title: 18 U.S.C. § 207
pinpoint: Subsections (a) and other provisions as applicable to individual candidate facts
proposition: Former-government personnel may face particular-matter and representation restrictions; hiring and assignment require individualized review.

title: Congressional Research Service, Protection of Classified Information by Congress: Current Practices, RS20748, May 29, 2026; primary CRS report mirrored by EveryCRSReport
pinpoint: Printed pages 3-5; Security Clearances for Staff; House Committee Staff. Canonical official product: https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/RS20748
proposition: Congress has formal safeguarding and staff clearance processes; clearance and access are not automatic consequences of prior executive-branch service. Full report date and text verified; mirror hosts the primary CRS document.
